In Rafael's family in Buenos Aires, the Sunday lunch always ended the same way. His aunt would say, "Yosef is going to be a doctor. And Rafael? You'll never be like your cousin."
Rafael heard it for years. By fifteen, he'd stopped trying in science. "I'm not the smart one," he'd shrug. "Yosef is."
Only his mother said differently. Every night she asked, "What did you try today?" When he fixed the neighbour's radio, she said, "See? You keep going till it works."
Slowly, Rafael started staying late in the school workshop. He began to think of himself as someone who fixes things.
